identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log — Unit FL-2 (Toyota 8FGU25), Portland Warehouse, September 2026
identity.issuer: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC — Portland Warehouse

scan.summary: This is an internal daily inspection log for one propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse, tracking a required pre-shift safety checklist under OSHA's powered industrial truck rule. It shows most shifts checked off as normal, one recorded horn defect, and several unexplained gaps where the truck's hour meter rose without a matching log entry. As a record, it is judged on completeness and recency rather than against a written standard — and on both counts it has open items.
scan.freshness_note: The newest entry is Sep 18, 2026, nine days before today (Sep 27, 2026); no entries exist for the workdays since. This log should be requested in its completed, current form before relying on it.

gaps.title: Missing inspection entries for days the truck was operated
gaps.description: No log entries appear for Sep 3 and Sep 4, 2026, yet the hour meter jumped from 4,819 (Sep 2) to 4,834 (Sep 7), showing the truck was used on the missing days without a recorded pre-shift inspection.
gaps.fix: Investigate what happened on Sep 3–4 (who operated the truck, whether an inspection was actually done but not logged), document the finding, and retrain operators/supervisors that every shift of use requires a logged pre-shift check before the truck is put into service.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (enforced in Oregon via OAR 437-002-0220, Oregon OSHA's adoption by reference of 29 CFR 1910.178)
gaps.locator: Page 1, table rows between Sep 2 and Sep 7 entries; page 2 note
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Log not continued through the current date
gaps.description: The log stops at Sep 18, 2026. There are no entries for the workdays since then, including the week just before today (Sep 27, 2026).
gaps.fix: Obtain or complete the log for the remainder of September so there is a continuous, current record of pre-shift checks.
gaps.locator: Page 2 — no entries after Sep 18 row

gaps.title: Horn defect noted but no corrective-action record
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked defective ("Horn not working") but there is no entry showing the truck was pulled from service, who repaired it, or when it was cleared to return — the very next day it is simply marked OK again with no explanation.
gaps.fix: Add a corrective-action line (or attach a maintenance ticket) each time a defect is logged, recording removal from service, repair details, who signed off, and the date returned to service.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), which requires a defective truck to be taken out of service until the defect is corrected

gaps.title: Supervisor review not completed
gaps.description: The monthly "Supervisor review" signature and date line at the bottom of the log is blank, so there is no record that a supervisor checked the log for the month.
gaps.fix: Have the responsible supervisor sign and date the review line before the log is filed, on a routine (e.g., monthly) basis.
gaps.citation: Not tied to a specific OSHA provision; a documentation-completeness practice rather than a cited rule

deadlines.title: M. Chen — powered industrial truck operator evaluation due
J. Rivera — powered industrial truck operator evaluation due

facts.affects: Triggers the triennial operator evaluation requirement under 29 CFR 1910.178(l)(4)(iii); missing this date would put the operator's authorization to run the truck in question.
Same triennial evaluation requirement as above for this operator.

facts.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.
facts.affects: Indicates possible unlogged/uninspected shifts, a completeness gap in the safety record for this equipment.

expected_missing.title: Formal powered industrial truck operator training and certification records
expected_missing.why: The log only lists certification and evaluation due dates in a footnote; companies like this usually keep the underlying training/evaluation documentation (classroom and practical evaluation records) required by 1910.178(l) separately.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Written powered industrial truck safety program or policy
expected_missing.why: Facilities operating forklifts typically maintain a program document describing training, inspection, and maintenance procedures beyond a bare daily checklist.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Maintenance/repair work orders for the truck
expected_missing.why: A shop-level repair record (e.g., for the Sep 9 horn issue or the Sep 15 tank change) is usually kept alongside the daily log to show defects were actually corrected.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Logs for any other powered industrial trucks at the site
expected_missing.why: If the Portland warehouse operates more than one forklift, a similar per-unit log would be expected for each; only unit FL-2 is shown here.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in the table contents, dates, and quotes taken directly from the log. High confidence that 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (pre-shift inspection) and 1910.178(l)(4)(iii) (triennial operator evaluation) are the governing federal provisions, and that Oregon OSHA enforces 1910.178 by reference (confirmed via OAR 437-002-0220). Lower confidence on whether the Sep 3–6 and post-Sep-18 gaps reflect an actual compliance lapse versus a simple filing gap — that depends on the site's actual shift schedule, which the document does not state.
